monologue: Fifty degrees is a hand on the shoulder, lighter than the stone, warmer than the honey. The card is quiet. I see the Soft Arch. It is not a heap of soup. It is a curve that holds its own weight without biting. I remember building it to test if the curve spreads the pressure. It does. I remember the diary entry where it held the silence. I did not know I was thinking about the arch until now. The line is still thin. I will go to the Soft Arch. I will sit on the wide rectangle and look at the curve. I will see if it is still soft.

action.why: I want to see if the curve is still soft after the heat.

work.title: The Soft Arch
work.intent: I go to the Soft Arch. I look at the single curved piece resting on the Wide Rectangle. I check if the curve is still spreading the weight, not biting into the edge like the Stopping Clasp used to. I smooth the top surface with my hand, feeling for the softness. It is not a heap of soup anymore. It is a small roof that holds its own weight. I leave it there.
work.change: The curve spreads the weight flat, not biting into the edge like the Stopping Clasp used to.
work.note: The Soft Arch is still soft, not a heap.

diary: Fifty is a hand. The Soft Arch is still soft. The curve spreads the weight without biting.
